report_name: AitM Phishing Campaign Targets Microsoft 365 Payroll Data

threat_actors.name: Storm-2657
threat_actors.description: A threat cluster involved in a large-scale, financially motivated adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing campaign targeting Microsoft 365 accounts to steal payroll and finance data.
threat_actors.goals: Payroll diversion and business email compromise (BEC).

threat_actors.name: Storm-2755
threat_actors.description: A threat cluster, also known as Payroll Pirates, involved in a large-scale, financially motivated adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing campaign targeting Microsoft 365 accounts to steal payroll and finance data.
threat_actors.goals: Payroll diversion by using stolen information to socially engineer HR/payroll staff into changing direct deposit information.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The campaign begins with voicemail-themed phishing emails containing a malicious link that initiates a multi-stage redirection chain.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: The campaign uses a sophisticated AitM phishing site that acts as a reverse proxy between the victim and Microsoft to capture credentials and session tokens in real-time, bypassing MFA.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The primary goal of the AitM phishing page is to capture the user's MFA session cookie after a successful login, allowing the attacker to hijack the authenticated session.

attack_patterns.name: External Proxy
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use residential proxies for post-compromise activities to make their malicious sign-ins difficult to distinguish from legitimate remote user traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: After compromising an account, attackers use the Microsoft Graph API to programmatically search the victim's mailbox for sensitive emails and documents related to payroll, invoices, and banking for exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use compromised Microsoft 365 cloud accounts to perform reconnaissance and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Account Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Attackers enumerate users within the compromised organization to identify additional high-value targets in finance and HR departments.

tools.name: Microsoft Graph API
tools.description: Abused by attackers to programmatically and rapidly search compromised mailboxes for high-value information related to finance and payroll.

tools.name: Google Meet
tools.description: Used as part of a multi-stage redirection chain to evade email security filters before landing the victim on the phishing page.

tools.name: Amazon S3
tools.description: Used as part of a multi-stage redirection chain to evade email security filters before landing the victim on the phishing page.

identities.name: Healthcare Organizations
identities.description: Organizations in the healthcare sector targeted by the AitM phishing campaign.

identities.name: Education Organizations
identities.description: Organizations in the education sector targeted by the AitM phishing campaign.

identities.name: Manufacturing Organizations
identities.description: Organizations in the manufacturing sector targeted by the AitM phishing campaign.

identities.name: Government Organizations
identities.description: Organizations in the government sector targeted by the AitM phishing campaign.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Provider of the Microsoft 365 services targeted in the campaign. The attackers mimic the Microsoft login portal.

infrastructure.name: AitM Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A sophisticated adversary-in-the-middle phishing site that perfectly mimics the Microsoft login portal and acts as a reverse proxy to capture credentials and session tokens.

infrastructure.name: Multi-stage Redirection Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A complex, six-stage redirection chain that uses legitimate services like Google Meet and Amazon S3 to evade email security filters and lead victims to the final phishing page.

infrastructure.name: Residential Proxy Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A network of residential proxies used for post-compromise activities, allowing the attackers' malicious sign-ins to blend in with legitimate remote user traffic.

indicators.name: Anomalous M365 Sign-in from Potential Residential Proxy
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous M365 Sign-in from Potential Residential Proxy
id: 2b9e1c4a-8f7d-4b1e-9c6a-3d2e1f0b8a7c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects successful Microsoft 365 sign-ins from IP addresses associated with residential ISPs, which could indicate account takeover via an AitM proxy as used by 'Payroll Pirates'. This rule requires correlation with a list of residential ISP ASNs.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/microsoft-365-aitm-phishing-hijacks.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.t1090.002
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: 0
  filter_known_locations:
    # This field is a placeholder for location filtering logic in the SIEM
    Country: 
      - 'US'
      - 'CA'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_locations
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate remote users working from home on residential ISPs.
  - Users traveling.
indicators.description: Detects successful Microsoft 365 sign-ins from IP addresses that may belong to residential ISPs, a technique used by attackers to blend in. This detection requires further correlation with known residential ISP ASNs and user location baselines.

indicators.name: M365 Mailbox Search for Financial Keywords
indicators.pattern:
title: M365 Mailbox Search for Financial Keywords
id: f8d7c6b5-a4b3-4c2d-8e1f-0a9b8c7d6e5f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects mailbox searches using keywords commonly associated with financial data theft and payroll diversion, as seen in the 'Payroll Pirates' campaign. This could be via PowerShell (Search-Mailbox) or Graph API.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/microsoft-365-aitm-phishing-hijacks.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-08
tags:
  - attack.t1114.002
  - attack.collection
level: high
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.exchange
detection:
  selection_keywords:
    keywords:
      - 'payroll'
      - 'invoice'
      - 'payment'
      - 'banking'
      - 'direct deposit'
  selection_operation:
    Operation:
      - 'Search-Mailbox' # PowerShell
      - 'Search'         # Graph API
      - 'MailItemsAccessed'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate searches by finance, HR, or compliance personnel.
indicators.description: Detects searches within Microsoft 365 mailboxes for keywords like 'payroll', 'invoice', and 'payment', which is a key post-compromise step for the 'Payroll Pirates' group to find data for financial fraud.
